scope: Separate Root-requested partial-write trait contract assessment; does not expand terminal cancellation repair or claim current successful workflow corruption

observation.claim: ChannelWriter::write can enqueue one or more chunks and then return Err from a later control.check or reserve branch without returning the prior accepted byte count. The fatal-kind-only repair intentionally does not change this structure.
observation.write_contract_basis: Root-provided std::io::Write contract: an Err reports no bytes written by that call. No standard-library source/doc fetch or runtime validation was performed by this agent.
observation.actual_workflow_assessment: Current production routes wrap ChannelWriter in BufWriter; export write_all/serde/flush propagate fatal errors. Sticky cancellation/closed queue prevents a productive later retry, and worker/body terminal paths report abort/failure rather than complete EOF. No successful corruption, duplicated-positive-output or automatic retry workflow after ConnectionAborted is established by this source audit.
observation.existing_positive_oracles: Old full-body successful EOF tests remain byteexact and still require actual future execution.

open_followup.possible_narrow_direction: Return Ok(accepted_prefix_bytes) when a later chunk fails after positive progress, preserving sticky terminal state so a subsequent write/flush reports the fatal error; keep zero-progress failures as Err. This is only an implementation direction, not an authored/approved fix.
required_validation: Actual controlled positive prefix enqueue then later cancellation/consumer close
write returns the actual nonzero accepted prefix, next write/flush fails terminally
No duplicated prefix under direct write retry or BufWriter behavior
Existing complete EOF/hash, 8queue/9thfull, actual worker/supervisor joins, body-drop and cancellation oracles unchanged
